chapter_name: Accounting for Partnership Firms - Basic Concepts
learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the financial rules of going into business with friends! Learn how to share profits, pay interest on capital, and handle disputes.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: It is the relation between two or more persons who have agreed to share the profits of a business carried on by all, or any of them acting for all.

This is the written agreement containing the terms and conditions of the partnership (like who gets how much salary, or the profit-sharing ratio). If there is no deed, the law says profits must be shared EQUALLY.
After a firm calculates its Net Profit, it needs a special account to show how that profit is distributed among the partners (as salary, interest on capital, and remaining profit share).

Under the Fixed method, you maintain two accounts per partner (Capital A/c and Current A/c) so the core capital never changes. Under the Fluctuating method, everything (salary, drawings, profit) gets dumped into one single Capital Account.

fun_activity.title: ⚖️ The Absent Agreement
fun_activity.instructions: Pretend you and a friend start a business but forget to sign a contract. You did 90% of the work and brought 80% of the money. According to the Indian Partnership Act 1932, how much profit do you get? (Spoiler: It's exactly 50/50. Always sign a deed!)

exam_tips: 📌 Rule of Absence: If there is no Partnership Deed, NO interest on capital, NO salary, and NO interest on drawings is allowed. But Interest on Partner's Loan is strictly given at 6% p.a.
📌 When calculating Interest on Drawings made uniformly throughout the year, use the Average Period Method (e.g., 6.5 months for beginning of every month).
📌 'Charge against profit' (like Rent paid to partner or Interest on Partner's Loan) goes to the regular P&L A/c, NOT the P&L Appropriation A/c.
quick_recap: ⭐ A partnership requires at least 2 people (maximum 50).
⭐ P&L Appropriation Account shows the distribution of profits among partners.
⭐ Past Adjustments are made via a single journal entry to fix errors from previous years.
